subject: computer-science

moments.title: Church's lambda calculus and the Church-Turing thesis
moments.body: Church publishes 'An Unsolvable Problem of Elementary Number Theory', using lambda calculus to give a different but equivalent definition of effective computability. Turing demonstrates the equivalence in his 1936 paper.
moments.takeaway: Two completely different formalisms — lambda calculus and Turing machines — define exactly the same set of computable functions. This is the Church-Turing thesis.

now.title: Functional programming today
now.body: Lambda calculus is the direct ancestor of LISP, Haskell, ML, F#, Scala, and the functional features added to JavaScript, Python and Java. The 2010s adoption of map/filter/reduce in mainstream languages is a delayed mainstreaming of 1936 mathematics.
now.open_questions: Is the Church-Turing thesis fundamentally a statement about physics or about mathematics? Quantum computing extends it (BQP rather than P), but does not violate it.

reflection: Turing was Church's PhD student at Princeton in 1936-38. The relationship between supervisor and student produced two of the foundational papers of computer science within months.
